updates.name: Stephen A. Montzka
updates.bio: Senior scientist at NOAA's Global Monitoring Laboratory in Boulder, Colorado. He makes and interprets multi-decade, high-precision gas chromatography-mass spectrometry records of more than 30 trace gases from sites worldwide, work that revealed an unexpected rise in emissions of the banned ozone-depleting gas CFC-11. He also studies hydroxyl-radical variability, carbonyl sulfide budgets and U.S. trace-gas emissions.
updates.research_interests: ozone-depleting substances; greenhouse gases; hazardous air pollutants; atmospheric oxidizing capacity (hydroxyl radical) and the methane budget; carbonyl sulfide and terrestrial photosynthesis; stratosphere-troposphere exchange; national- and state-scale U.S. trace-gas fluxes; CFC-11 emissions and Montreal Protocol compliance

updates.bio: Research hydrologist with the USDA Forest Service Northern Research Station; Ph.D. 2008, SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry. His publications link catchment hydrology and biogeochemistry, including mercury export, peatland carbon cycling under experimental warming in the SPRUCE experiment, and long-term records from the Marcell Experimental Forest and Sleepers River Research Watershed.
updates.research_interests: ecosystem biogeochemistry; catchment science; nitrate source tracing; hydrology

updates.name: Stephen R. Carpenter
updates.bio: Emeritus Professor of Integrative Biology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison who directed its Center for Limnology from 2009 to 2017 and still holds a scientist title. His lake research joins biogeochemistry with food-web processes, covering trophic cascades, land-water interactions and human effects such as fishing and exotic species, tied to the North Temperate Lakes LTER; he also studies social-ecological resilience.
updates.research_interests: interaction of biogeochemistry and food-web processes in lakes; trophic cascades; land-water interactions and prediction of lake characteristics; effects of fishing and exotic species; resilience of linked social-ecological systems

updates.name: Steven C. Pennings
updates.bio: Moores Professor in the Department of Biology and Biochemistry at the University of Houston and director of the UH Coastal Center. A plant community ecologist, he uses coastal wetlands' steep salinity and flooding gradients to test how stress, disturbance and species interactions structure salt marshes, mangroves and coastal prairies, including mangrove range expansion and plant-herbivore interactions.
updates.research_interests: salt-marsh, mangrove and coastal-prairie plant community ecology; physical stress and disturbance gradients; marsh-to-mangrove transitions and wetland function; plant-herbivore interactions across space and time; parasitic plants; oil-spill impacts on coastal wetlands; long-term ecological research

updates.name: Steven H. D. Haddock
updates.bio: Senior scientist and marine biologist at the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute and adjunct professor of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at UC Santa Cruz. He studies deep-sea and open-ocean gelatinous zooplankton such as comb jellies, siphonophores, medusae and radiolarians, covering their bioluminescence, diversity, ecology and evolutionary relationships, and isolates new light-producing and fluorescent proteins. Ph.D., UC Santa Barbara.
updates.research_interests: bioluminescence; deep-sea and open-ocean gelatinous zooplankton (ctenophores, siphonophores, radiolarians, medusae); biodiversity and ecology; phylogenetics of gelatinous taxa; cloning of novel photoproteins and fluorescent proteins
